answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by locking a bond for 24 epochs and requiring six independently audited tasks before full rewards unlock. A walnut scheduler randomly assigns reviewers and prevents a sponsor from selecting its own panel. An onyx registry stores signed output fingerprints; matching clusters lose 30 percent of their bond. A karst rate limit allows only two new identities per sponsor each epoch. Thus fake identities require capital, audit exposure, and patience, while every decision remains reproducible from task hashes and attestations.
